sections.label: Arrests and asset seizures
sections.summary: Ten persons were arrested and charged for offences including laundering overseas criminal proceeds, and their seizeable Singapore assets were seized.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Ten persons were arrested and charged for offences, including laundering proceeds from overseas criminal activities, and their seizeable assets in Singapore were seized.

sections.label: Seized assets total value
sections.summary: Police said assets seized or issued prohibition of disposal orders total more than $2.8 billion, including properties, vehicles, monies, cash, cryptocurrencies, gold, bags, watches and jewellery.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On 20 September, Police updated that the total value of assets seized or issued with prohibition of disposal orders stood at more than $2.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To date, the total value of assets seized or issued with prohibition of disposal orders by the Police stands at more than $2.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This includes: Prohibition of disposal orders issued against 152 properties and 62 vehicles with a total estimated value of more than $1.24 billion, as well as thousands of bottles of liquor and wine; And seizures of monies in bank accounts amounting to more than $1.45 billion; cash, including foreign currencies, amounting to more than $76 million; cryptocurrencies of more than $38 million; 68 gold bars, 294 luxury bags, 164 luxury watches and 546 pieces of jewellery.

sections.label: Largest anti-money laundering operation
sections.summary: The case is described as one of the largest anti-money laundering operations in Singapore and likely the world.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In summary, this case is one of the largest anti-money laundering operations not just in Singapore, but likely the world.

sections.label: US Department of Justice seizure
sections.summary: The US Department of Justice announced its largest financial seizure of more than US$3.5 billion, about $4.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In February last year, the United States (US) Department of Justice announced its largest financial seizure to date of more than US$3.5 billion, which is equivalent to about $4.8 billion.

sections.label: Assets seized or prohibited
sections.summary: Assets amounting to more than $240 million were seized or prohibited.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Assets amounting to more than $240 million were seized or prohibited.

sections.label: MAS prohibition orders and penalties
sections.summary: MAS issued prohibition orders to 11 individuals, penalties of $3.8 million to three banks and an insurer, and seven individuals were charged, three convicted.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MAS issued to 11 individuals prohibition orders ranging from three years to lifetime bans from working in Singapore's financial sector for their gross misconduct.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Three banks and an insurer in Singapore were issued penalties amounting to $3.8 million for failure to perform customer due diligence (CDD) and to adequately establish the sources of wealth of high-risk customers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Seven individuals have been charged in relation to this case.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Three of them have been convicted for offences including money laundering.

sections.label: Singapore FATF presidency
sections.summary: Singapore currently holds the presidency of the Financial Action Taskforce.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Internationally, Singapore currently holds the presidency of the Financial Action Taskforce (FATF).

sections.label: Enforcement against PSPM dealers
sections.summary: Since 2021, 96 enforcement actions were taken against PSPM dealers for failing CDD and cash transaction reporting requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To the question by Assoc Prof Razwana, since 2021, 96 enforcement actions have been taken against PSPM dealers for failure to comply with CDD and cash transaction reporting requirements.

sections.label: STRs received by STRO
sections.summary: STRO received an average of 43,000 STRs annually between 2020 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: STRO received an average of 43,000 STRs annually between 2020 and 2022.

sections.label: Money laundering convictions and seizures
sections.summary: From 2020 to 2022, at least 240 individuals were convicted of money laundering, and Police seized over $1.2 billion in investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 2020 to 2022, at least 240 individuals were convicted of money laundering offences, largely for laundering domestic scam proceeds.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In that same period, Police seized more than $1.2 billion worth of assets in money laundering investigations.

sections.label: SPF seized bank account funds
sections.summary: During investigations, the Singapore Police Force seized over $750 million from several bank accounts in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the course of the investigations, Singapore Police Force (SPF) seized over $750 million from several bank accounts in Singapore.

sections.label: Financial institutions AML/CFT breaches
sections.summary: In the past five years, 17 financial institutions were taken to task for breaching MAS' AML/CFT requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the past five years, 17 financial institutions had been taken to task for breaches of MAS' AML/CFT requirements.

sections.label: Applicants not on Red Notice
sections.summary: At the time of their applications, none of the applicants were on INTERPOL's Red Notice.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the time of their applications, none of them were on INTERPOL's Red Notice.

sections.label: FATF 2016 Singapore assessment
sections.summary: In its 2016 evaluation, the FATF assessed Singapore to have a strong legal and institutional framework against ML/TF.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In its last evaluation of Singapore in 2016, the FATF assessed Singapore to have a strong legal and institutional framework against ML/TF.

sections.label: Inter-Ministerial Committee on AML regime
sections.summary: An Inter-Ministerial Committee led by Indranee Rajah will strengthen the anti-money laundering regime, with related Ministerial Statements and clarifications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As I mentioned, we have been undertaking ongoing reviews in the various sectors, to tighten our anti-money laundering regime.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Learning from this case, we will consider further measures to strengthen our regime.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second Minister for Finance Indranee Rajah will be leading an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) involving the relevant sectoral regulators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Later in her speech, she will outline its terms of reference and priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will strengthen trust and confidence among investors and Singaporeans, that we run a clean system that stands among the tallest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister of State Alvin Tan and Minister Indranee Rajah will be making related Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on three Statements after the third Statement is made.

sections.label: MAS review of SFO tax incentives
sections.summary: MAS is reviewing its internal incentive administration processes and will tighten them, having already announced plans in July 2023 to strengthen surveillance against SFO money laundering risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Ongoing investigations and supervisory engagements suggest that one or more of the accused persons in this case may have been linked to SFOs that were awarded tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: At the point of application, no adverse information of note related to the individuals and entities had surfaced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, MAS is reviewing our internal incentive administration processes and will tighten them where necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: More broadly and even before this case, MAS had already in July 2023 announced plans to strengthen its surveillance and defence against potential money laundering risks posed by SFOs.

sections.label: ACIP collaboration and Agritrade conviction
sections.summary: The ACIP is a key platform for collaborating with the financial industry, with efforts bearing fruit such as the conviction of Agritrade International's former CFO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As Minister Teo mentioned earlier, the ACIP is one key platform through which we collaborate with the financial industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: These efforts, too, have borne fruit, for example, with the conviction of the former Chief Financial Officer of Agritrade International for her role in deceiving financial institutions to grant at least $776 million in credit facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On 17 January 2023, she was sentenced to an imprisonment term of 20 years.

sections.label: COSMIC expansion and launch timeline
sections.summary: MAS is working expeditiously on COSMIC and is on track to launch it in the second half of 2024, if not earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim, Miss Rachel Ong and Mr Derrick Goh asked if MAS can consider expanding participation in COSMIC beyond financial institutions to include additional parties, as well as whether we can expedite the launch of COSMIC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that we are now working really expeditiously on COSMIC and are on track to launch it in the second half of 2024, if not earlier.

sections.label: COSMIC scope and sharing limits
sections.summary: There are no plans to extend COSMIC beyond the financial sector or to share COSMIC information directly with overseas institutions or international counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: At this stage, there are no plans to extend COSMIC to entities beyond the financial sector, or for COSMIC information to be shared directly with financial institutions overseas or with international counterparts.

sections.label: 1MDB AML/CFT penalties
sections.summary: In the 1MDB case, penalties were imposed for AML/CFT violations, some individuals and senior management were permanently banned, and two banks were closed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In the 1MDB case, we imposed significant penalties for AML/CFT violations, permanently banned some individuals and senior management from working in Singapore's financial sector, and even closed down two banks for egregious AML/CFT breaches.

sections.label: Seized assets and MAS reviews
sections.summary: More than $1.45 billion in financial assets have been seized, and MAS is conducting supervisory reviews and inspections of financial institutions with a major nexus to the case.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The fact that more than $1.45 billion in financial assets have been so far seized in relation to this case is concerning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: MAS is conducting detailed supervisory reviews and inspections of the financial institutions with a major nexus to this case.

sections.label: MAS assessing AML/CFT practices
sections.summary: MAS will assess whether financial institutions upheld robust AML/CFT practices, including checks on customers' sources of wealth and funds, transaction monitoring and mitigating ML/TF risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: MAS will assess whether financial institutions had upheld robust AML/CFT practices, including performing adequate checks on their customers' sources of wealth and funds, monitoring customer transactions to pick out suspicious ones and taking all reasonable steps to mitigate against ML/TF risks.

sections.label: Prohibition orders on residential properties
sections.summary: 94 residential properties have been issued prohibition orders, comprising 60 completed resale units and 34 uncompleted units sold directly by developers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To date, 94 residential properties have been issued with prohibition orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Of these, 60 are completed resale units and 34 were uncompleted units sold directly by developers.

sections.label: PR landed property approvals
sections.summary: In 2020, 2021 and 2022, 24, 51 and 34 approvals were granted each year to PRs to own landed residential property on Singapore mainland.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2020, 2021 and 2022, 24, 51 and 34 approvals were granted in each year respectively to PRs to own landed residential property on Singapore mainland.

sections.label: Raised ABSD rate for housing
sections.summary: In April 2023 the rate was raised from 30% to 60% to dampen investment and prioritise Singaporean owner-occupation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In April 2023, this was raised from 30% to 60% as part of pre-emptive measures to dampen local and foreign investment and prioritise Singaporean owner-occupation.

sections.label: Anti-money laundering rules for property
sections.summary: Property agents' duties were legislated in 2021, and 2023 changes extended anti-money laundering requirements to developers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While there had been practice guidelines in place prior, in 2021, we legislated the prescribed duties of property agents with the introduction of the Estate Agents (Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism) Regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2023, we introduced changes to the Housing Developers (Control and Licensing) Act and the Sale of Commercial Properties Act to also extend anti-money laundering requirements to developers of residential, commercial and industrial properties.

sections.label: Cash ban for uncompleted property sales
sections.summary: Developers are not allowed to accept cash payment for uncompleted property sales.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For uncompleted property sales, developers are not allowed to accept payment in cash.

sections.label: Regulators of real estate sector
sections.summary: CEA regulates property agents and agencies, while URA regulates developers in the real estate sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the real estate sector, the Council for Estate Agencies (CEA) is the regulator which oversees the property agents and agencies while the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) regulates the developers.

sections.label: Investigations into money laundering property transactions
sections.summary: Investigations are ongoing into agencies and agents who facilitated transactions for properties in the money laundering probe, with regulatory action if breaches are found.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Investigations are ongoing into the property agencies and agents who had facilitated transactions for the properties involved in the money laundering probe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will fully investigate the incident and if any breaches are found, take the necessary regulatory action.

sections.label: ACRA screening and resident director rule
sections.summary: ACRA screens company officers and shareholders against adverse information lists, and companies must have at least one Singapore-resident director.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: When a company is incorporated, ACRA screens all the officers and shareholders in its registers against lists of known adverse information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, all companies are required to have at least one director resident in Singapore, to ensure that we will be able to hold someone accountable for any breaches committed by the company in Singapore.

sections.label: Companies struck off
sections.summary: About 17,000 such companies have been struck off over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: About 17,000 such companies have been struck off over the last five years.

sections.label: ACRA sanctions on filing agents
sections.summary: Between 2021 and 2023, ACRA imposed 24 sanctions against Registered Filing Agents, including eight cancellations or suspensions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2023, ACRA imposed 24 sanctions against Registered Filing Agents, including eight cases where the Registered Filing Agent's registration was cancelled or suspended.

sections.label: Proposals tabled in Parliament
sections.summary: The proposals had undergone public consultation earlier and are to be tabled in Parliament in early 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The proposals had undergone public consultation earlier and we are looking to table them in Parliament in early 2024.

sections.label: Directors holding few directorships
sections.summary: 99% of directors hold fewer than 10 directorships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Having said that, 99% of directors hold fewer than 10 directorships.

sections.label: Beneficial owners filing with ACRA
sections.summary: Companies will be required to identify their beneficial owners and file this information with ACRA to address cloaking of ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: A third area, which Mr Don Wee asked about, is to address the cloaking of the ownership of companies and the identity of money launderers through the use of complex corporate structures, by requiring companies to identify their beneficial owners and file this information with ACRA.

sections.label: IMC reviewing anti-money laundering system
sections.summary: An IMC of political office holders from MAS, MHA, MinLaw, MOM and MTI, chaired by the speaker, will review the system in four main areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, we will be setting up an IMC comprising political office holders from MAS, MHA, the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and chaired by myself to review our system with the benefit of what we are learning from this case and to keep our regime up-to-date with increasingly sophisticated crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The review will focus on four main areas: first, on how we can better prevent corporate structures from being abused by money launderers; second, how financial institutions can enhance their controls and collaborate more effectively with each other and authorities to guard against and flag suspicious transactions; third, how other players in the system, like corporate service providers, real estate agents and precious stones and metals dealers can help to better guard against money laundering risks; and fourth, how we can centralise and strengthen monitoring and sense-making capabilities across Government agencies to better detect suspicious activities.

sections.label: Singapore clean trusted business hub
sections.summary: Singapore is determined to preserve its hard-earned reputation as a clean and trusted business hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Singapore is determined to preserve our hard-earned reputation as a clean and trusted business hub.

sections.label: Seizing assets and FATF standards
sections.summary: Seizing high value assets deprives criminals of oxygen and deters money laundering; FATF sets global standards Singapore subscribes to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Seizing and confiscating such high value assets in one fell swoop is tantamount to depriving criminals of "oxygen", thereby decisively crippling their activities constitutes, in my view, the best deterrent against anti-money laundering activities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In her speech, she referred to the FATF as setting the global anti-money laundering standards and that Singapore, as a member, subscribes to these standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand that the FATF has conducted mutual evaluation of Singapore's anti-money laundering standards to gauge compliance with its 40 recommendations to tackle illicit financial flaws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: How have we fared in these mutual evaluations as far as the abilities and the enforcement records of our enforcement agencies are concerned, and how do we compare to the abilities of enforcement agencies in other major financial centres, such as in London or New York?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But understandably, all the work that goes into our anti-money laundering regime is quite involved.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, with your permission, Sir, may I ask the Clerks to distribute a handout which describes more fully the different aspects of our anti-money laundering regime?

sections.label: Singapore FATF membership since 1992
sections.summary: Singapore has been a member of FATF since 1992.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By way of background, for Members' information, Singapore has been a member of FATF since 1992.

sections.label: Mutual evaluation audit schedule
sections.summary: Mutual evaluation is involved and irregular; Singapore was last audited in 2016 and next in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Because this is a very involved exercise to carry out a mutual evaluation, countries do not get to be audited so regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We were last audited through this mutual evaluation in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The next time we go through mutual evaluation is, in fact, in 2025.

sections.label: Singapore ranked 100 of 128
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked 100 out of 128 among those considered lowest risk.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Singapore was ranked 100 out of 128, amongst those that are considered to be lowest risk.

sections.label: Withholding enforcement grew asset value
sections.summary: Withholding enforcement until a fuller picture emerged grew the assets from $1.8 billion to $2.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In this particular instance, if we had not made the decision to withhold enforcement action until as full a picture emerged – we might have been able to, say, sometime in 2022 or the earlier part of 2023 gone after the suspects – we might not have gotten what was initially $1.8 billion, which grew to $2.4 billion and now $2.8 billion.

sections.label: Warning to money launderers
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore is resolved to catch money launderers who try to flow dirty money through it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This ability to uncover a web of this size is actually something that speaks volumes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, if you are a money launderer, if you still think that Singapore is a good place to try and flow your dirty money through, please know that we are equally resolved to catch you.

sections.label: MAS supervision and bank complicity
sections.summary: MAS supervisory engagements continue, and MAS will act firmly against financial institutions and individuals if it finds complicity or collusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In this case, and also, in speaking to Member Raj Thomas' view, MAS' supervisory engagements with financial institutions, underpinned by all of the different procedures, regulations and preventions, are ongoing in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We will constantly review whether there had been any lapses in the AML/CFT regime in accordance with our process and our policies and also whether any of these lapses had been incurred in onboarding the accused persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Where there has been complicity on the part of the relationship manager, for example, or senior management, in onboarding the accused persons, I want to assure all Members that if MAS finds any complicity or collusion by banks or their staff, we will not hesitate to take firm actions against the financial institutions and individuals involved to hold them accountable.

sections.label: Non-banking intermediaries and gatekeeper training
sections.summary: Non-banking financial intermediaries are where banks were 15 years ago, and sectoral regulators provide red flag indicators and gatekeeper training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: In many ways, one feels that the non-banking financial institution intermediaries are where banking institutions used to be 15 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We do have a set of red flag indicators that each sectoral regulator provides to their community of gatekeepers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clearly, it is also in our interest to ensure that the training of the gatekeepers is properly done so that they, like Mr Neil Parekh said, also ask their customers the right questions and their minds are correctly attuned to the potential risks.

sections.label: Highest cash transaction reported
sections.summary: A Member asks the maximum cash amount reported by institutions through the suspicious transaction reporting system, but the matter is a live investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, can I ask Minister Indranee, so far what was the maximum amount of cash that was reported by the institutions – whether financial institutions or whether the integrated resorts (IRs) or public companies – the highest amount of cash transaction reported by IRs, banks and property companies through the suspicious transaction reporting system.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But as I explained during my Ministerial Statement, this is a live investigation.

sections.label: STR numbers and sources
sections.summary: 43,000 STRs were filed on average annually between 2020 and 2022, with 80% from financial institutions and 20% from other gatekeepers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think I should answer it because it relates to the STRO.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned in my Statement that 43,000 STRs were filed on average annually between 2020 and 2022, 80% of them came from the financial institutions, 20% came from the other non-financial institution gatekeepers that would include corporate service providers, that would include property agents and other types of gatekeepers.

sections.label: STR confidentiality
sections.summary: STRs are confidential by nature and their contents are not generally disclosed because this is a live investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: No, there is nothing that I would like to add except to say one other thing, which is that the STRs, by their nature, are confidential.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Insofar as anybody is asking what does an STR contain, this is not information that is generally disclosed in any event because it is part of the investigation and this is a live investigation.

sections.label: Financial sector GDP and workers
sections.summary: Minister Josephine said the financial sector contributes about 14% to GDP and 200,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I listened to Minister Josephine's speech just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: She mentioned about the financial sector contributing about 14% to GDP and 200,000 workers.

sections.label: IMC capacity building comparison
sections.summary: The question asks Minister Indranee how IMC capacity building for agencies like MAS compares with other financial hubs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: An additional question is to Minister Indranee: in the IMC, in terms of capacity building for agencies in relation to the financial sector like MAS, how do we compare – in terms of staffing and amount spent on capacity building comparing to other financial hubs like New York, London, Hong Kong and other jurisdictions as well?

sections.label: MAS Anti-Money Laundering Department
sections.summary: MAS established the dedicated Anti-Money Laundering Department in 2016 for anti-money laundering supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On anti-money laundering resources, the MAS' approach to the supervision of anti-money laundering and the countering of financial terrorism, is that it has established the dedicated department, that is the Anti-Money Laundering Department (AMLD), in 2016.

sections.label: AMLD staffing and surveillance tools
sections.summary: The AMLD has 40 staff and MAS uses data analytics and network analysis tools for money laundering and terrorist financing surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The AMLD currently has 40 staff and they work very closely with other departments to tackle money laundering as well as terrorist financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I wanted to assure the Member and also Members of this House that MAS has in fact been building up these capabilities and at present are using data analytics and network analysis tools to conduct system-wide money laundering and terrorist financing risk surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It is really our approach to continue to review and enhance these surveillance capabilities, including with the money laundering and terrorist financing information when we launch and we roll out COSMIC, which allow greater sharing of information amongst financial institutions.

sections.label: IMC centralising monitoring capabilities
sections.summary: A key IMC focus is centralising and strengthening monitoring and sensemaking capabilities across Government agencies to detect suspicious activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, increasingly, it is going to become technology and analytics that pull together all the information that different people in this system submit up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I think, to answer his question, when we set up the IMC, one of the key areas of focus that I talked about was, how we can centralise and strengthen monitoring and sensemaking capabilities across Government agencies to better detect suspicious activities.

sections.label: Sector GDP and jobs share
sections.summary: The sector accounts for 14% of GDP and 200,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As we mentioned earlier on, the sector accounts for 14% of our GDP as well as 200,000 jobs.

sections.label: Foreign regulators AML fines
sections.summary: The US, UK, Switzerland and Hong Kong imposed fines and warnings on their financial institutions for AML/CFT control failures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Other financial regulators have also had to deal with the cases and Minister Teo had mentioned that in her main reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But the US, the UK, Switzerland and Hong Kong also imposed fines and warnings against their financial institutions for respective failures in AML/CFT controls.

sections.label: COSMIC information sharing platform
sections.summary: COSMIC is being developed to let financial institutions share customer information crossing risk thresholds and later expand to other risk areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We know that there is a particular weakness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And therefore, as I mentioned earlier on, we are developing COSMIC to allow financial institutions to share information on customers that specifically cross certain risk thresholds and to then allow them to break down these information silos more effectively, so that you are able to detect and disrupt criminal activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In subsequent phases, as mentioned earlier, we will expand COSMIC to include other risk areas and even more financial institutions.

sections.label: MAS tightening measures, terminating incentives
sections.summary: MAS is tightening measures as necessary and will look to terminate these incentives as appropriate while investigations continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As investigations are ongoing, I cannot reveal more than what I had said in my Parliamentary reply earlier on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, what I can say is that MAS is tightening these measures as necessary, and we will be looking to terminate these incentives as appropriate.

sections.label: Charities filing suspicious transaction reports
sections.summary: Charities have a legal obligation to file an STR if they know or suspect property or transactions are connected to criminal activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The answer to the first question is it is a legal obligation to file an STR if charities know or, in fact, have grounds to suspect that the property or transaction that they are dealing with is connected to criminal activity.

sections.label: Aligning incentives at IMC
sections.summary: At the IMC, aligning incentives matters because the $2.8 billion quantum may lead people to wrong conclusions about money laundering in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I think, most importantly, when we get to the IMC is to look at aligning of incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think when people look at the very large, staggering quantum of the $2.8 billion in this case, they might draw the wrong conclusion about the state of money laundering in Singapore or the adequacy of our regulatory regime.

sections.label: Regulating gatekeepers better
sections.summary: The regime is strong, but gatekeepers like lawyers, accountants and real estate agents can be better regulated through prevention, detection and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And this is testament to the strength and robustness of our regulatory and enforcement regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And I think what we have been outlining here today, is that we have been saying that we can do better in regulating gatekeepers like the lawyers, accountants, real estate agents, especially through prevention, detection and enforcement as well as other prongs of our anti-money laundering strategy.

sections.label: STR filing questions
sections.summary: The speaker repeats questions asked in each of the last three years about STRs filed on property transactions, AML/CTF involvement and prosecutions for failure to file STRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I will just repeat the salient points of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I asked in each of the last three years how many STRs were filed with regard to property transactions and how many of such property transactions were later found to be involved in AML/CTF activities, and lastly, how many individuals were prosecuted for a failure to file STRs when they should have?

sections.label: Property agents accessing foreign background data
sections.summary: The question asks whether property agents can access background information on foreign individuals from 43,000 STRs, or get limited access to COSMIC, RTIG or a similar portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can property agents access detailed background information on foreign individuals, including their businesses, wealth sources and red flags from the 43,000 STRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If not, can MAS grant them limited access to COSMIC, RTIG or another similar portal for better due diligence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What will this webpage provide and when will it be ready?

sections.label: SLA anti-money laundering checks
sections.summary: SLA does not carry out additional anti-money laundering checks on transactions because this would duplicate existing CDD checks by real estate agents, developers and agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer is, SLA does not carry out additional anti-money laundering checks on transactions because this would duplicate the existing CDD checks by real estate agents, developers and agencies.

sections.label: CEA action against property agents
sections.summary: CEA will act against property agents or agencies breaching the EAA or PMLFT regulations, with penalties up to $100,000 for agents and $200,000 for agencies, and has taken action against two agents since 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The short answer is that the CEA will not hesitate to take action against property agents or agencies, who are found to have breached the EAA or the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (PMLFT) regulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And those who fail to comply with the regulations can face disciplinary action, including financial penalties of up to $100,000 for property agents and $200,000 for property agencies and suspension or revocation of an agent's registration or an agency's licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Since 2021, CEA has taken action against two property agents who were found guilty by the CEA disciplinary committee for contraventions of the EAA and the PMLFT regulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the most recent case, the property agent was imposed with a financial penalty of $400,000 and had her registration suspended for four months in July 2023.

sections.label: Family offices in case
sections.summary: The question asks how many family offices were involved and how MAS will strengthen the regulatory regime, with investigations suggesting accused persons may have been linked to SFOs awarded tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In this case, how many family offices were involved and how will MAS strengthen the regulatory regime for family offices?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I said that ongoing investigations and supervisory engagements suggest that one or more of the accused persons in this case may have been linked to SFOs that were awarded tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I also shared with Ms Usha Chandradas earlier that MAS is looking to tighten these checks and that we will be looking to terminate these incentives, as appropriate.

sections.label: SFOs linked to case
sections.summary: SFOs linked to this case represent a very small proportion of all SFOs here, and a completed consultation will enable tightening of processes while remaining open to talent, investments and financial flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: SFOs linked to this case, in fact, represent a very small proportion of all the SFOs here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have just completed the consultation, which will enable us to tighten some of these processes, but we remain open as the other Ministers and I have mentioned – to talent, to investments as well as to financial flows, including those in SFOs.

sections.label: Prohibition orders on properties
sections.summary: 94 residential, 53 commercial and five industrial properties were issued prohibition orders, with eight landed residential properties at Sentosa Cove and no mainland landed residential properties purchased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The third question: are there any landed properties on mainland Singapore among the non-prohibited properties?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I said, to date, 94 residential properties have been issued with prohibition orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then, in addition to that, there are 53 commercial properties and five industrial properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Member's other question was: was there any landed residential property on the mainland that was issued with the prohibition order?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I said that out of the 94 residential properties, 60 were completed resale units, 34 were uncompleted units and eight of these properties were landed residential properties at Sentosa Cove.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, there were no mainland landed residential properties purchased.

sections.label: Employment Pass applications approved
sections.summary: Employment Pass applications were approved because individuals met prevailing salary and qualification requirements, companies provided supporting documents, and no INTERPOL Red Notices were issued at application time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Specific to the recent money laundering incident, the Employment Pass applications were approved to these individuals because they met the then-prevailing work pass requirements on salary and qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: When asked for the proof of business operations and the ability to pay salaries, the companies which submitted the applications were able to provide supporting documents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At the time of their Employment Pass applications, none of the Persons of Interest had INTERPOL's Red Notices issued against them.

sections.label: Minister Indranee leading IMC
sections.summary: Minister Indranee said she will lead an IMC to keep the regime up-to-date with increasingly sophisticated crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Minister Indranee shared in her speech that she will be leading an IMC to ensure that our regime remains up-to-date with increasingly sophisticated crimes.

sections.label: Singapore business environment ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked the world's best business environment by the Economist Intelligence Unit in the second quarter of 2023, and checks should be strengthened without closing doors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the second quarter of 2023, Singapore is ranked the world's best business environment by the Economist Intelligence Unit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This strong performance is in line with many other global rankings on economic competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is a hard-earned reputation that has taken us years to achieve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And as I have said earlier, the vast majority of work pass holders come to Singapore to work and to contribute to our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We should not let a handful of individuals or "black sheep" taint the economic contributions of the majority and start closing our doors or giving the impression that we are doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In fact, this is exactly why we need to be targeted in strengthening our checks so that we can take action on unscrupulous individuals and on companies while maintaining a business-friendly environment for the vast majority that want to invest in Singapore and to create good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: There is a recent article in the Financial Times that alluded to this phenomenon that companies are increasingly wanting to domicile or headquarter their businesses in Singapore as they see Singapore as a trusted and neutral jurisdiction where they can avoid the geopolitical sensitivity and the Financial Times termed this as "Singapore-washing".

sections.label: Singapore AML/CFT regime
sections.summary: The same interconnectedness characteristics attracting investors also attract illicit criminals, and Singapore's robust AML/CFT regime is in line with FATF standards and compares well with other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And the same characteristics which investors as well as companies consider when they invest in Singapore are the same characteristics, interconnectedness, that illicit criminals and syndicates also are attracted to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And we have also said that Singapore has a very robust AML/CFT regime that is in line with FATF standards, for example, and our regime compares well with other countries.

sections.label: Bank fines proportionality question
sections.summary: Minister Josephine Teo mentioned $3.8 million in fines on three banks, and the question asks whether this penalty is proportional to profits banks can make on $1.45 billion still in the bank account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: One, Minister Josephine Teo mentioned that $3.8 million of fines had been imposed on three banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The question I want to ask the Minister of State is: is this penalty proportional to the amount of profit that the banks can make on the $1.45 billion which is still in the bank account?

sections.label: AML/CFT investigations of financial institutions
sections.summary: In the last five years, 20 investigations were opened against financial institutions for suspected AML/CFT breaches, with enforcement actions against 17.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the last five years, we had a total of 20 investigations that were opened against financial institutions for suspected breaches of AML/CFT requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And these enforcement actions were taken against 17 financial institutions.

sections.label: Investigations of individuals
sections.summary: A total of 25 investigations were opened against individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In addition, a total of 25 investigations were opened against individuals.

sections.label: COSMIC information sharing thresholds
sections.summary: Under COSMIC, information sharing is allowed only when customers cross stipulated thresholds guided by financial crime red flags in pre-defined risk areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Under COSMIC, I assure the Member, that information sharing will only be allowed when customers cross stipulated thresholds for sharing, which are primarily guided by financial crime red flags in pre-defined risk areas – and, currently, it is related to shell companies, trade-based money laundering and proliferation financing.

sections.label: Sources of STRs
sections.summary: STRs came from a variety of gatekeepers, including banks, corporate service providers and real estate agents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On her first, in relation to the STRs, they came from a variety of gatekeepers and the usual gatekeepers that are involved include the banks, they include corporate service providers, they include real estate agents – and so there is a variety.

sections.label: Foreign law enforcement cooperation and foreign company exemption
sections.summary: The speaker cannot disclose which foreign law enforcement agencies are involved, and asks if the Government will review exempting foreign companies holding only property from beneficial ownership information.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Specific to this case, I am not at liberty to disclose which foreign law enforcement agencies we are working with.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Because the proceeds that potentially had been laundered through the Singapore system involve activities that were carried on outside of Singapore; they could involve more than one jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And as we cast our net wide, it would not be unusual or unthinkable for us to be cooperating with other law enforcement agencies – not confined to one country, China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: First, in relation to her Statement regarding the anti-money laundering regime applicable to foreign companies in Singapore, may I ask if the Government is minded to review its decision to exempt foreign companies which hold only property in Singapore and not carrying other forms of business here, from the requirement to provide beneficial ownership information?

sections.label: Wirecard and seizure amounts
sections.summary: Mr Leong conflated the $3.8 million, related only to the Wirecard incident, with the $1.45 billion in seizures of monies in bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Leong was not right to, in the first place, conflate the $3.8 million with the $1.45 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The $3.8 million is related only to the Wirecard incident.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With respect to the $1.45 billion, I had said in my Statement that these are seizures of monies in bank accounts amounting to more than $1.45 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This money does not belong to the bank.

sections.label: Firm action against errant banks
sections.summary: Fines and other measures like banning institutions, revoking licences and holding senior management to task are invoked, but guilt should not be attributed prematurely while investigations continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Fines are one, but we have invoked other measures, including banning financial institutions, revoking their licences, as well as holding senior management to task.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As what Minister Josephine Teo had mentioned earlier on, the investigations are ongoing; we cannot, and we ought not to prematurely attribute any guilt or offence to the banks prematurely until investigations have been completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But I want to assure the Member and assure Members of the House that we take firm action against errant banks, against errant financial institutions and against the senior management of financial institutions if they are found wanting and if they are found to have contravened our strict AML/CFT standards, which are, as I mention again, aligned with international standards and verified and assessed by FATF.

sections.label: Inferring bank involvement criticised
sections.summary: It is not right to infer the involvement of banks and financial institutions in this case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Because if that is not the case, then today, you can tell me what are the total fines imposed on our banks already.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think it is not right for him to infer as to the involvement of the banks and financial institutions in this particular case.

sections.label: Leong's inference on banks
sections.summary: It is not right for Mr Leong to infer, though he acknowledged he may have misunderstood by saying banks were complicit.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is not right for Mr Leong to infer in his last part of his clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think it is helpful that he acknowledged that he may have misunderstood by saying that the banks were complicit.
